title: Checkpoint: The Lives of Stars
objective: After this level you can trace a star’s life from nebula to its final state based on its mass.
summary: Mass decides everything: Sun-like stars end as white dwarfs, while the most massive leave neutron stars or black holes.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 finale. One number decides a star’s whole life story.
cards.body: That number is its mass. Everything in this chapter, from nursery to final glow, follows from it.

cards.headline: Two paths
cards.body: A star’s final fate depends mainly on its mass. A Sun-like star takes the gentle road: it swells into a red giant, sheds a planetary nebula and settles down as a white dwarf. A star far more massive than the Sun takes the loud road: it explodes as a supernova and leaves behind something much stranger, a neutron star or a black hole. Same universe, very different retirement plans.
cards.callout: Sun-like → white dwarf · Massive → neutron star or black hole

cards.headline: A Sun-like star’s life, start to finish

events.label: Collapses from a cold, dense cloud of gas and dust
Fuses hydrogen into helium for billions of years
Core runs low on hydrogen; outer layers swell
Sheds a planetary nebula; a white dwarf remains and slowly cools

questions.prompt: What measures a nearby star’s distance directly?
questions.explanation: Parallax, the shift as Earth orbits, gives a nearby star’s distance directly.

questions.prompt: How will a Sun-like star end its life?

options.label: As a black hole
options.rationale: That takes a far more massive star.

options.label: As a neutron star
options.rationale: That takes a far more massive star.

questions.explanation: A Sun-like star sheds its outer layers and leaves a white dwarf.

questions.prompt: Which stars have the shortest lives?

options.label: The most massive, hottest and brightest ones
The smallest, coolest red dwarfs
options.rationale: Red dwarfs can shine for trillions of years.

options.label: The youngest stars
options.rationale: Age doesn’t set lifespan; mass does.

questions.explanation: More mass means a hotter, brighter star with a shorter life. The most massive last only a few million years.

questions.prompt: What decides whether a star ends as a white dwarf or explodes as a supernova?

options.label: Its distance from Earth
options.rationale: Distance only changes how bright it looks.

options.label: The number of planets it has

questions.explanation: A star’s mass decides its fate: Sun-like stars become white dwarfs; the most massive explode as supernovae.

questions.prompt: Chapter 7 recap: which order follows a Sun-like star through its life?

options.label: Red giant → nebula → main sequence → white dwarf
options.rationale: The red giant comes after the main sequence.

options.label: Cloud of gas → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf
White dwarf → red giant → main sequence

questions.explanation: Born from a cloud, a Sun-like star spends billions of years on the main sequence, swells into a red giant, and ends as a white dwarf.
